title: AMD Instinct MI50/MI60 and Radeon VII (gfx906) with mx-llama.cpp
examples: Two or four MI50 32GB in an x86 server
One MI50 on an RK3588 board (single GPU: no tensor parallelism)

general.summary: mx-llama.cpp, a llama.cpp fork tuned for gfx906 (weight repack, tensor parallelism across GPUs), built with HIP.
general.notes: Load with direct I/O (load_mode dio): mmap hangs with this fork. Several GPUs: split mode 'tensor'; Tensor parallel GPUs (-tps) sets how many form each group (0 = all in one), and must divide the GPU count. Its peer-write AllReduce stays off (GGML_ENABLE_CUSTOM_AR=0) until scripts on your host show peer-to-peer access works; turn it on to compare. Never set HSA_FORCE_FINE_GRAIN_PCIE=1 on a host without cache-coherent PCIe, such as RK3588. ROCm: official ROCm 7 images no longer ship rocBLAS kernels for gfx906; use ROCm 6.x, or build it (the mi50-arm guide on ARM). Check the build against the CPU with llama.cpp's test-backend-ops before trusting its answers (mi50-arm's gpu-parity.sh does this).

notes: Untested on real hardware. cett-dump and the server activations patch build into the fork (checked on the CPU backend).
